analyst_view.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games, while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points and in poor form at home and away (lost 1-3 at Artis Brno in the league on 21 Nov and went out of the Czech cup to the same side on 11 Nov). Lugano also lead the Swiss Super League and beat Grasshopper 2-1 on 21 Nov after a 5-0 loss at St. Gallen before the break; coach Mattia Croci-Torti has said the league is the priority, and this trip opens a run of five away games in 15 days (Luzern, St. Gallen in the cup, FC Zurich, Copenhagen). RSI reported on 8 Nov that Dereck Moncada and Ilija Delcroix were injured and keeper Amir von Ballmoos went off with a back problem; the numbers list no absentees for either side, and I could not confirm whether the three are back. No referee is named yet and team news was thin, so the view rests mainly on Lugano's schedule and those injuries.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with both sides at about 1.6. I lean slightly lower to about 3.0: Lugano may rotate with five away games in 15 days and the league as Croci-Torti's priority, and Moncada (a scorer in the 4-0 over Luzern) was injured as of 8 Nov, which the numbers don't know. Jablonec's thin scoring lately is already in their momentum figure.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec at home. Lugano's recent corners are already counted (slightly below expected), and nothing I found on tactics or lineups points either way, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.9 cards and already push both sides up for recent card-heavy games (Jablonec +9%, Lugano +5%). Ajeti's red card at St. Gallen was in the league, so it does not change this match, and no referee has been named yet; I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots. A mild lean lower to about 29.8, for the same reason as goals: a likely rotated Lugano side and Moncada's injury reported on 8 Nov, neither of which the numbers see. Jablonec's recent shot counts are already in momentum.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I trim it to about 8.8 because Lugano may field a changed attack with Moncada doubtful and a busy away run ahead; the numbers already count Lugano's sharp recent finishing (35 on target in six).
